subject: SIG follow-up: Clarification on runtime ephemeral logs and training policy
messages:
From: Lori Chen <lori.chen@clearwellhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@clearwellhealth.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up — ephemeral logs / training on customer data

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the SIG spreadsheet you sent last week. Our security team dug into the answers and asked for a couple of clarifications before we close the questionnaire:

1) Do runtime prompt logs (including KV cache / prefix caching metadata) persist to durable storage anywhere in the hosted or private deployments by default? If so, where and for how long?
2) Does Redwood ever use customer prompts or payloads to train or improve models? If yes, please specify opt-out controls and whether this applies to dedicated or private deployments as well.
3) Can you provide a high-level evidence pack for the ephemeral logging architecture and a redacted SOC 2 excerpt that references logging retention controls?

We'd like short, concrete answers and any artifacts (diagram, excerpt, or audit ID) we can include with our vendor review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our procurement deadline for vendor approval is 2027-06-10.

Best,
Lori Chen
Senior InfoSec Manager
Clearwell Health

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Lori Chen <lori.chen@clearwellhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 10:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — ephemeral logs / training on customer data

Hi Lori — thanks for the precise questions. Short answers up front, detailed notes and artifacts attached below.

1) Runtime prompt logs and prefix/KV cache: By default, Redwood hosted API treats per-request token streams as ephemeral. We do capture short-lived telemetry (latency, error traces) and anonymized service metrics. Prompt bodies and KV cache are not persisted to durable customer-visible storage in hosted by default. For debugging incidents, ephemeral traces can be materialized for a narrow window (configurable, default 24 hours) and require elevation to access.

2) Training on customer prompts: Redwood does not use customer prompt or payload data to improve or retrain models by default for any production tier. Hosted API customers may opt into an analytics/training program with explicit consent and contract amendments; Dedicated and Private deployments never have data used for model training unless the customer explicitly configures an opt-in pipeline.

3) Evidence: attached a redacted SOC 2 excerpt and an architecture diagram that highlights our ephemeral telemetry path and access controls. I'll also attach the completed SIG sheet (v1) with the cells cross-referenced.

Next steps: Marissa will follow up on procurement-specific questions and Karthik can provide the exact audit IDs and retention config flags if you need them for our vendor form. If you want a short recorded walkthrough of the artifact, we can schedule 20 minutes this week.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_sig_answers_v1.xlsx (SIG answers); soc2-report-redacted-2026.pdf (redacted SOC 2), runtime-telemetry-architecture-diagram.png

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lori Chen <lori.chen@clearwellhealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — ephemeral logs / training on customer data

Hi Lori — quick note from procurement side: for Clearwell's vendor form we normally need the retention fields filled as a single-line answer we can paste into our template. Could you confirm the exact default retention window for ephemeral traces and provide the config flag names for Dedicated/Private?

Per Soojin: default ephemeral trace materialization window = 24 hours (config: runtime.trace_materialize_window_hours). For hosted customers who enable extended debug traces, max retention is 30 days but it requires SOC2-certified access controls and a documented incident justification. Dedicated pools are configurable by the customer; default on Dedicated is 0 (no prompt persistence) unless the customer enables "debug-trace-collector". Private deployments have no outbound collection by default — any log/export requires an installation-time opt-in.

I'll paste this into Clearwell's vendor form unless you want to tweak wording.

Thanks,
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — ephemeral logs / training on customer data

Thanks — that's helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we move to approval: 

- Can you confirm whether any customer data is ingested into long-term analytics stores used for model quality monitoring (examples: aggregated prompts used to build prompt-level feature datasets)? If Redwood does this for any customers, what anonymization steps are applied and where is the dataset hosted?
- For the Dedicated option: please confirm whether the "debug-trace-collector" requires an explicit service account and that it can be disabled by policy. We need a statement we can include in the vendor agreement that the feature is opt-in and requires customer admin activation.

If possible please include a short snippet we can put in the MSA around no customer data used for training unless explicitly opted-in via a written amendment.

Best,
Lori

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lori Chen <lori.chen@clearwellhealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 23:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — ephemeral logs / training on customer data

Hi Lori — following up with the precise confirmations Soojin referenced and some suggested MSA language below. Short answers: 

- Long-term analytics / model quality datasets: Redwood may collect aggregated, metadata-only telemetry and labeled evaluation results into long-term analytics stores for platform monitoring and model performance evaluation. These collections do not, by default, include raw customer prompt text or customer payloads. Any process that does include prompt content requires explicit opt-in and is covered by a documented contract amendment. When customers opt-in, Redwood applies a multi-stage redaction and hashing pipeline (PII redaction, token-level hashing) before storing any content. Hosted analytics datasets are hosted in our encrypted analytics cluster (us-east-1) with KMS-managed keys; Dedicated analytics exports are tenant-isolated on the customer's dedicated pool if requested.

- Dedicated debug-trace-collector: Confirmed opt-in only. The collector requires an administrator-created service account with a scoped role (role: debug_trace_collector) and cannot be enabled by support without documented customer authorization. The feature is disabled by default and can be turned off via the Dedicated pool policy (config: dedicated.debug_trace_collector_enabled = false).

Suggested MSA snippet you can paste into your vendor form: 

"Redwood Inference will not use Customer content (including prompts, files, or API payloads) to train, fine-tune or improve models, except where the Customer expressly opts-in via a signed amendment. If the Customer opts in, Redwood will apply documented redaction and hashing procedures and host any resulting datasets in tenant-isolated storage with customer KMS support as agreed in the amendment."

I've attached the completed SIG answers workbook and the SOC2 excerpt referenced earlier — happy to add any additional citations.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Platform Trust
Redwood Inference
